profile.org_note: Six reportable homebuilding regions since Q1 2026 (Pacific Northwest, California, Desert, Mountain, Texas, East; Q3 2026 10-Q segment note), each a group of brand divisions; this replaced the FY2025 three-region layout (West, Mountain, East) after Woodside, Holt and Chesmar were merged in, and the CEO is the sole chief operating decision maker. Regional presidents run division operations (land, construction, sales) and report up to corporate in Denver; divisions source land through Division VPs of Land Acquisition, but every real estate acquisition must be approved by the real estate Asset Management Committee (CEO David Viger, CFO Robert Martin, the Chief Legal Officer, two Sekisui House, Ltd. representatives and at least one other corporate officer). No corporate land chief is published; treasury sits with VP, Treasurer Clare Wilson under the CFO. A sister company, North America Sekisui House, LLC (NASH, Arlington VA), invests in land and master-planned communities and is linked from shus.com, but is not part of Sekisui House U.S. in the filings.
profile.summary: Seventh- or eighth-largest US builder (11,712 closings and about $6.4 billion of revenue in 2025), wholly owned by Japan's Sekisui House and built on the former M.D.C. Holdings platform, selling in 14 states under Richmond American, Woodside, Holt, Chesmar, Hubble and SHAWOOD. It is land-heavy: 35,216 lots controlled at 2025-12-31, of which 28,728 owned and only 6,488 (about 18%) optioned, and the parent's FY2026-28 plan names 'land acquisition methods to enhance ROA' as a US priority while targeting 13,600 deliveries in 2028. It still files voluntarily with the SEC (may stop at any time), which is the main public window into its officers and debt.

gaps: Regional presidents, land VPs and treasury hires: trade press and local press were not searched. The gaps below marked 'not searched' are not confirmed absences.
Regional president for California: not publicly disclosed (no 2025-2026 source names the holder).
Regional president for Desert (AZ, NV, NM): not publicly disclosed.

Regional president for Mountain (CO, UT): not publicly disclosed. The previous Mountain regional president, Natasha Gandhi, left to become CEO of View Homes (Builder, 2026-03-10), and the company advertised a Denver-based 'Regional President, Mountain' role afterwards (third-party job boards). Whether it has been filled is not public.

Regional president for Texas: not publicly disclosed. A 'Regional President, Texas Division' posting (Dallas/San Antonio, overseeing the Texas division presidents) was live in early 2026 and is now closed; the hire was not announced. Ken Trainer (Chesmar COO and governing person of Chesmar Holdings, LLC in the Texas Comptroller's 2025 record) is a lead but is not confirmed as region head.
Regional president for East (FL, MD, TN, VA): not publicly disclosed. Jack Gallagher was Richmond American's Mid-Atlantic and Florida regional president in 2020 (row added as an Inferred lead only).

Corporate head of land (Chief Land Officer, EVP/SVP or national VP of land, CIO): not publicly disclosed. Filings name no land officer; land approvals sit with the real estate Asset Management Committee. 2026 postings show only division-level land seats (Division VP Land Acquisition in Houston/Dallas East, San Antonio/Austin, Boise and Folsom), and an 'Executive Vice President of Operations' posting covered land development enterprise-wide.

Regional reporting lines: the filings say only that the CEO is the chief operating decision maker; that regional presidents report to the CEO is inferred, and no COO has been named since January 2025.

Division land heads outside Holt (Richmond American, Woodside, Chesmar, Hubble divisions): not named on company sites; not searched. richmondamerican.com was down for maintenance on 2026-11-19, and the Woodside, Chesmar and Hubble sites publish no leadership pages.

Open land seats on the company careers site on 2026-11-19: Division Vice President, Land Acquisition (San Antonio / Austin) and Division Vice President, Land Acquisition & Development (Boise). Whether these are vacancies or new seats is not stated.

Chief Legal Officer: the title exists (member of the Asset Management Committee per the FY2025 10-K) but the holder is not named in the filings opened. Michael L. Kaplan resigned as Senior Vice President and General Counsel in June 2024.
Chief Operating Officer: none identified since David Viger moved from COO to CEO on 2025-01-01.
Chief Accounting Officer: Derek R. Kimmerle last confirmed in an October 2024 release; the Q3 2026 10-Q signature page could not be read (the fetch tool truncates the filing before the signatures).

Head of SH Residential Holdings, LLC (the direct parent): Toru Tsuji was its CEO in October 2024 and left the Sekisui House U.S. board on 2026-02-01; who leads it now, and Tsuji's current role, are not confirmed.

Roger Gannon (Woodside), Ken Trainer (Chesmar) and Rick Robideau (SH Services): titles are as of the parent's 2025-09-04 notice; their titles after the January 2026 One Company reorganisation are not confirmed.
Hubble Homes (Boise) and Chesmar division leaders: not named on their sites. Erin Willis (chief insights and marketing officer in 2023 trade press) was not re-confirmed and is left out.
